why.text: Cool, humid Atlantic summers and southerly winds ripen Hondarrabi grapes slowly, giving high-acid whites with citrus and herbal notes.

styles.text: Light, lightly acidic whites with citrus and herbal notes; also rosado, red and barrel-fermented white.

climate.text: Atlantic, humid and mild, with cool summers and mostly southerly winds at ripening; wines reach 10.5 to 11.5 % alcohol.

altitude.text: Vineyard land at or below 400 m, anywhere in Bizkaia.

why.text: Stony, slate-rich soils on steep slopes regulate rainwater, while cold winters and very hot summers shape these wines.

styles.text: Young and oak-aged reds and whites; fruity, with floral notes and, when aged, spice and toast.

climate.text: Low winter temperatures, very hot summers and a long frost period.

soil.text: Stony soils with abundant slate, on steep slopes.

why.text: Mild Atlantic climate, vineyards mostly by the sea, neutral soils and 1,600 mm of rain give txakoli with high acidity.

styles.text: Fresh, light whites with a slight spritz; also rosado, red and barrel-fermented white.

climate.text: Mild Atlantic: about 1,600 mm of rain, mean 18 to 20 °C during ripening, south and southwest winds late in ripening.

soil.text: Neutral soils, with most vineyards close to the sea.

why.text: Slightly acid soil and an Atlantic climate with frequent south wind give round, low-acid txakoli with citrus and herbal flavours.

styles.text: Whites, rosados and reds, plus barrel-fermented white; whites show green apple and citrus, with a slight bitter finish.

climate.text: Atlantic; mean 13.1 °C (highs 18.7, lows 7.5) and south wind on about 170 days a year.

why.text: Humid Atlantic climate, poor, thin, acidic soils and pergola-trained vines shape the acid, aromatic Albariño that dominates the zone.

styles.text: Albariño and other whites, some oak-aged; also red and quality sparkling wine.

climate.text: Atlantic, close to the sea and humid.

soil.text: Low pH, poor in minerals and nutrients, and thin.

why.text: Steep terraces on slate and granite above the Miño and Sil canyons ripen Mencía and Godello in long, hot summers.

styles.text: Reds, whites and rosados, usually young, some aged in barrel; Mencía leads the reds, Godello the whites.

climate.text: More continental than Atlantic: long hot summers, mild autumns, 700 to 800 mm rain, mean 11.3 °C, strong winds.

soil.text: Alluvial soils over slate, with more granite in places.

why.text: Sloping, sometimes terraced vineyards in a Mediterranean-oceanic climate give structured Godello and red-fruited Mencía.

styles.text: Godello whites and Mencía reds; also quality sparkling wine and Tostado, made from raisined grapes.

climate.text: Mediterranean-oceanic climate; vines grow on slopes, sometimes steep terraces.

why.text: Temperate Atlantic climate with big day-night swings, little rain after fruit set and rugged, thirsty soils give fresh, balanced wines.

styles.text: Fresh whites and reds, plus Tostado, a naturally sweet wine from grapes dried indoors.

climate.text: Temperate Atlantic, with large day-night temperature differences and little rain from fruit set.

soil.text: Rugged, harsh soils with low water-holding capacity.

why.text: Low rain, hot summers and big day-night swings at ripening suit native grapes, giving floral, fruity, balanced wines.

styles.text: Whites and reds, young or aged in oak; whites floral and fruity, reds with red fruit and soft tannins.

climate.text: Low rainfall, high summer temperatures and strong day-night temperature swings during ripening.
